A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAGLE-3 work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original acceleration benchmarks, training-data scaling experiments, component ablations, and throughput measurements in Section 4 and Figures 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and adds SGLang throughput evaluations attributed to the collaborating SGLang team.

M1.justification: The training-time test, token prediction objective, multilayer feature fusion, and dynamic drafting procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A newly specifies EAGLE-3's tree depth; v1 did not state that setting, so this does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The training sources and five evaluation datasets remain unchanged. The added SGLang experiments reuse MT-bench and LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B, varying serving settings rather than data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: The added deployment comparisons introduce unmodified SGLang as an explicitly measured serving baseline, alongside SGLang with EAGLE or EAGLE-2 in Tables 3–4. The original benchmark comparator sets and vLLM comparison are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation in SGLang v0.4.4 on one H100, using chain length 3, batches through 64, and absolute throughput at batch size 1. These supplement the retained vLLM experiment with maximum chain length 2; they do not establish changes to the original benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: The new SGLang batch-size sweep extends the analysis of whether acceleration survives increased batching in an optimized serving framework. The component ablations, training-data scaling analyses, and acceptance-rate curves remain unchanged; Figure 7 receives an axis-label correction.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added throughput tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: New SGLang results include 1.38x throughput for EAGLE-3 versus 0.99x for EAGLE at batch size 64. Table 4 adds 158.34, 244.10, and 373.25 tokens/s for SGLang alone, with EAGLE-2, and with EAGLE-3. Tables 1–2 and v1 Table 3, retained as v3 Table 5, have identical results. These are additional settings, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The speculative-sampling acceptance and replacement equations, feature definitions, and conditional acceptance-rate definition are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The method, scaling-law, and maximum 6.5x acceleration claims remain. The abstract adds 1.38x SGLang throughput at batch size 64, while the introduction replaces its highlighted vLLM result through batch size 56 with the SGLang result, described there as 40% improvement.

C2.justification: v3 emphasizes effectiveness within highly optimized serving frameworks, and Appendix A explains that higher acceptance permits deeper draft trees. It removes v1's explicit warning against comparing the vLLM throughput results with differently configured experiments. The central mechanism explanations and model-size limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents EAGLE-3's depth of 8 versus EAGLE-2's 6, with unchanged node counts. v3 also specifies the SGLang version, hardware, target model, dataset, and drafting settings. Added vLLM hardware information is inconsistent: Section 4.4 says RTX3090, whereas Table 5 says A100. The code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Zheng et al. 2024 SGLang reference and modestly extends its positioning toward optimized production serving. The related-work discussion and distinctions from EAGLE, HASS, Medusa, and other speculative-decoding methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits update the abstract and contribution bullet, divide throughput discussion into SGLang and vLLM subsections, add acknowledgements and an appendix paragraph, and correct minor wording. The broader narrative, method exposition, and conclusion remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds two SGLang tables and retains the original vLLM table as Table 5 with an expanded caption. Figure 7 replaces the misleading 'Data scale' axis and 1–128 labels with 0-alpha through 7-alpha while retaining the curves. Other displays remain substantially unchanged apart from reflow.

improvement.justification: The SGLang evaluations provide useful additional evidence of practical acceleration, Appendix A fills an implementation-detail gap, and Figure 7 corrects a misleading axis. These gains preserve the original scientific evidence. The conflicting vLLM hardware descriptions and removal of the explicit cross-setting comparison caution limit the improvement, but the overall result is modestly stronger and clearer.
